text:
sofia: Ran cross-region precision matrix for new-7B (seq=1024, mixed-batch sweep). uploaded raw CSV + perf plots to s3://redwood-bench/new-7B/precision-matrix-2026-03-20.zip :point_up: TL;DR: INT8 gives ~1.8–2.3x throughput on H100 depending on kernel; FP8 matches BF16 quality and gives ~1.3–1.6x speedups on H100. A100 shows smaller INT8 wins (1.2–1.7x) because of kernel variance. Regions tested: us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1.

chen: awesome — can you paste the exact command and batch/seq settings you used? also which kernel flags?

sofia: sure — single-run example below (we ran this for each gpu/region/precision combo, 3 runs each):

```
rw-bench run \
  --model=new-7B \
  --precision=int8 \
  --gpu=h100 \
  --region=eu-west-1 \
  --batch=8 \
  --seq=1024 \
  --kernel=k_int8_h100_v2 \
  --warmup=50 \
  --steps=200
```

sofia: notes: - all runs use tokenizer cache warmup; - eval quality = EM/F1 on our longform QA devset (1.2k examples); - latency numbers are p50/p95 token latency measured by runner; throughput in tokens/sec aggregated over steady state.

ravi: pasted summary table from the CSV (rounded):
- us-west-2 / H100 / BF16: p50 34ms, p95 98ms, throughput 540 tok/s (batch=8, seq=1024)
- us-west-2 / H100 / INT8: p50 18ms, p95 62ms, throughput 1130 tok/s, speedup 2.1x vs BF16, quality delta EM -0.5%
- eu-west-1 / H100 / FP8: p50 25ms, p95 72ms, throughput 720 tok/s, speedup 1.33x vs BF16, quality delta EM -0.1%
- eu-west-1 / A100 / BF16: p50 40ms, p95 120ms, throughput 450 tok/s
- eu-west-1 / A100 / INT8: p50 28ms, p95 92ms, throughput 700 tok/s, speedup 1.56x vs BF16, quality delta EM -0.7%
- ap-southeast-1 / L4 / BF16: p50 60ms, p95 170ms, throughput 220 tok/s
- ap-southeast-1 / L4 / INT8: p50 38ms, p95 110ms, throughput 410 tok/s, speedup 1.86x vs BF16, quality delta EM -1.2%

mariana: interesting that L4 had a decent int8 gain — which kernel did you use there? last time L4 int8 was unstable.

sofia: L4 used `k_int8_l4_v1` from the community kernel pack; we applied per-layer clipping (scale tuning) which fixed instability for our model. logs: some outliers early but steady after warmup.

chen: what about end-to-end latency for chat use (streaming)? token-latency is great, but user-perceived latency matters. any p95 response times for 256 tokens?

ravi: for streaming experiments (simulate interactive: prompt=128 tokens + generate 256 tokens, chunk=64):
- H100 / INT8: p95 end-to-end 420ms (mostly generation), H100 / BF16: 820ms
- A100 / INT8: p95 560ms, A100 / BF16: 980ms
So INT8 halves E2E p95 on H100 in our test harness.

amal: nice. for capacity planning — if we expect 50 concurrent interactive sessions (avg qps ~12 requests/sec), recommend reserve: H100 dedicated pool of 6 gpus with 25% headroom for bursts (we used throughput->requests mapping and conservatively assume 10 k tokens/session). happy to share calc sheet.

bench-bot: auto-suggestion: reserve-policy: {"model":"new-7B","precision":"int8","pool_gpu":"h100","min_gpus":6,"headroom_pct":25} — posted to infra-benchmarks channel.

mariana: kernel notes: on H100 we saw `k_int8_h100_v2` > `xformers_int8` by ~15% throughput (less quant admin). on A100, `k_a100_int8_v3` gives best stable perf. For FP8 we used `fp8_native_h100` which gave best match to BF16 quality.

sofia: quality summary: average EM drop vs BF16 = INT8: -0.6% (range -0.2 to -1.2), FP8: -0.15% (range -0.0 to -0.4). our internal quality threshold is 1.0% absolute EM drop for blocking. so INT8 is ok for non-critical routes; FP8 looks safe for most traffic (esp. on H100).

chen: action items?
sofia: 1) run extended eval with 10k prompts (long-tail) for INT8 on A100 + L4 (assign @ravi), 2) add per-token latency hist to the perf dashboard and include p99 (assign @mariana), 3) add kernel flag auto-selection to the runner (RW-BENCH) for region+gpu combos (assign @chen).
